Record date: 2129-12-05
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/05/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent cough with yellow sputum, ongoing shortness of breath, and continued fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit one week after initiating treatment with Azithromycin and continuing Prednisone for his COPD exacerbation. He reports that while the frequency of his cough remains unchanged, he has noted a slight improvement in the quality of his sputum, which is now less purulent and more clear. However, he continues to experience significant shortness of breath, especially during activities of daily living, and his fatigue persists, impacting his overall quality of life. He denies fever or chills but mentions that his night sweats have decreased in frequency.
Mr. Fairfax has adhered to the medication regimen, including the increased doses of Salmeterol and Tiotropium. He reports using his nebulizer less frequently, now every 6 hours, as his wheezing has somewhat improved.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + productive cough with yellow sputum, + occasional wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 128/74 mmHg - Heart Rate: 78 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 28 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 87% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued but is in less respiratory distress compared to the previous visit.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Mild wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with some rhonchi present.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with partial response to current treatment; persistent cough and shortness of breath warrant further optimization of therapy. 2. Improvement in sputum characteristics suggests possible resolution of an underlying bacterial infection. 3. Congestive heart failure remains stable; no signs of fluid overload or exacerbation.
PLAN
1. Continue Azithromycin 500 mg daily for a total of 10 days to ensure complete resolution of any potential bacterial infection. 2. Maintain oral Prednisone 20 mg daily for one additional week to further manage inflammation associated with COPD exacerbation. 3. Continue Salmeterol at 100 mcg twice daily and Tiotropium as prescribed; monitor for any adverse effects or need for further bronchodilation. 4. Reassess the use of Fluticasone/Salmeterol inhaler to ensure optimal control of respiratory symptoms; consider increasing dosage if symptoms persist. 5. Schedule a follow-up appointment in one week to evaluate clinical progress, including symptom resolution and any need for additional interventions. 6. Educate Mr. Fairfax on recognizing signs of exacerbation and the importance of adherence to the medication regimen. Encourage continued light physical activity and the use of his nebulizer as needed.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with the current medication regimen, including a continuation of Azithromycin and Prednisone. He was advised to maintain regular follow-up and to report any worsening of symptoms immediately. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for one week from today to reassess his condition and adjust the treatment plan as necessary based on his clinical response.
